summary: Intro discovery to align on Elmwood's inference budget constraints and decide between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated or Private. Discussed per-token pricing sensitivity, batching and KV/prefix caching levers, residency and encryption (KMS), and proposed a short pilot with benchmarks.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Jared Thompson (Elmwood Head of ML), Priya Rao (Elmwood Director of Platform), Emily Zhang (Elmwood Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Elmwood are early into rollout of LLM features for their research assistants; primary constraints are monthly budget cap for inference, latency SLOs for interactive UIs, and strict encryption KMS requirements. They want recommendation between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private and to see unit economics using batching/caching and quantization.

---
00:00 Jared: hey everyone, thanks for doing this, we wanted to make sure we get a clear picture of the numbers and options today.
00:08 Aisha: yep, thanks for the time. i'll kick off with a quick agenda: scope, current stack, constraints, then carlos will deep dive on batching/caching levers, and we can decide pilot next steps. sound good?
00:15 Priya: sounds good.
00:18 Carlos: cool, i'll try to keep it high level then dive into the knobs.
00:22 Jared: quick context — we're building an internal research assistant used by product and sales teams, about 150 daily active users but some spikes. current model is a 7B open model hosted in-house on GCP instances. Latency's okay for now but costs are climbing and our infra team wants to understand if it's cheaper to transfer to a managed hosted API or reserved dedicated capacity.
00:40 Aisha: perfect, exactly the tradeoff we help customers quantify. first question — what's your current monthly inference budget or a cap you can't exceed?
00:47 Priya: rough cap is $25k/month for this feature initially, maybe increasing after Q3 if adoption grows.
:53 Carlos: okay, and do you have a target p99 latency for interactive flows?
00:56 Jared: p95 around 400-500ms is fine for most flows; some priority flows need <250ms.
01:04 Carlos: good, that helps. also, how variable is QPS — do you have steady volume or big diurnal spikes?
01:10 Jared: spikes — sales demos cause short bursts up to 60 qps, average is 12 qps.
01:16 Aisha: noted. two important levers we usually talk about: batching (improves throughput but adds per-request latency) and KV/prefix cache (reduces repeated generation cost if prompts re-use prefixes). carlos will show examples.
01:27 Carlos: right — so basic per-token cost depends on model size, quantization, and serving mode. Hosted is straightforward per-token; Dedicated can lower per-token if you commit capacity; Private has higher fixed infra cost but can be cheaper at scale and meets residency/KMS requirements.
01:43 Priya: on KMS — we need customer-managed KMS for any PII or proprietary prompts. will Redwood Private support an HSM-backed KMS?
01:51 Carlos: yes, Private supports customer KMS and HSM integrations, and we can show audit log flow. Hosted can integrate with external KMS for keys at rest? small caveat: Hosted is multi-tenant so we have envelope encryption but not customer-managed HSM unless we move to a Dedicated/private contract.
02:07 Emily: is SOC2 available for hosted?
02:09 Aisha: hosted is SOC2 compliant; we'll send the attestation and the security pack.

02:15 Carlos: ok back to economics — quick worked example: assume 7B model, with baseline unquantized float inference on a T4-class GPU vs quantized int8 on a32x VF — numbers are illustrative: Hosted per-token list price might be $0.0008 per token, Dedicated reserved capacity could drop that to $0.00045/token depending on commitment, and fully private on customer infra can be as low as $0.0003/token but you pick up infra ops.
02:42 Jared: those ranges are helpful. our main question — with our QPS profile and 25k budget, which mode gets us closest to the latency targets while staying within budget?
02:52 Carlos: quick back-of-envelope: if you average 12 qps and average response is 100 tokens, that's 12*100*3600*24*30 = 3,110,400 tokens/month. at $0.0008/token that's $2,488/month — hmm wait that math seems low, we probably mis-multiplied — hold on.
03:15 (interruption, brief crosstalk)
03:18 Carlos: sorry, i'm confusing per-second vs per-request. simpler: 12 requests/sec * 100 tokens/request * 60 * 60 * 24 * 30 = 311,040,000 tokens/month. at $0.0008 that's $248,832/month — too high. at $0.00045/token it's $139,968/month. at $0.0003/token it's $93,312/month. so with a $25k budget, raw per-token model charges alone blow past the budget.
03:50 Priya: wow that's a lot higher than we thought, that explains the infra team's concern.
03:54 Aisha: this is where batching and caching shift the math. if you can batch requests you increase throughput per GPU and reduce per-token billing dispersion, and with prefix or KV cache you avoid recomputing repeated contexts. for interactive UX, small batching windows (20-50ms) can get you most gains without blowing the latency budget.
04:12 Carlos: example: if you can batch to an effective 1.6x tokens/sec efficiency improvement for generation and cache 40% of prefix tokens for typical prompts then your effective token consumption drops dramatically. using the same numbers, 311M tokens * (1 - 0.4)/1.6 = about 116M billable tokens. at $0.00045/token that's about $52k/month — still >25k but much closer if you also use smaller model variants or stronger quantization.
04:43 Jared: So it sounds like we need a combination: quantization + batching + cache + maybe route low-priority requests to a cheaper fallback model.
04:52 Aisha: yes, and Redwood Optimize can suggest batching windows and quant profiles for your prompt mix. we can run a short eval on your prompt set to show expected reductions.
04:59 Emily: from procurement perspective we need clear caps and overruns visibility — can we set monthly spend caps on Hosted?
05:06 Aisha: yep Hosted has quota controls and alerts; Dedicated gives you committed throughput so cost predictability is better. also can set auto-fallbacks.
05:16 Priya: If we commit to Dedicated, what's the minimum term?
05:19 Carlos: usually 3- or 12-month reserved capacity. month-to-month is possible but higher unit price. we can model a 6-month pilot too.
05:27 Jared: what about splitting traffic? we want interactive flows on low-latency dedicated, while background batch jobs go to hosted or cheaper GPU pools. is that supported?
05:35 Carlos: absolutely, routing policies let you split by route, by latency SLA, or by priority. you can also have automatic fallback to smaller/faster variants when capacity is constrained.
05:43 Priya: you mentioned quantization tradeoffs — what's the quality delta between 4-bit and int8 for our models?
05:48 Carlos: depends on architecture; for many open 7B/13B models int8 keeps quality close for conversational tasks, but 4-bit may introduce some degredation on creative long-form. we should validate on your eval prompts.
05:58 Jared: can Redwood help run a quick AB on our prompts?
06:01 Aisha: yes, that's the pilot we recommend: we collect a representative prompt set, run hosted and dedicated configs with quant profiles, measure latency/throughput and a small quality eval. then produce a per-token cost projection.
06:13 Emily: timeline — how fast can we get pilot numbers?
06:16 Carlos: if you share prompts and QPS estimate by Wednesday, we can spin up a 5-day benchmark and get numbers within 10 business days.
06:24 Aisha: noted as an action item — jared to share prompt set and traffic shape.

06:30 (short pause)
06:33 Jared: another constraint — some of the prompts include PII and we need audit trails and Customer KMS. earlier you said Hosted doesn't support customer HSM; would that block us?
06:42 Carlos: you could do a hybrid: sensitive routes to Dedicated or Private with customer-managed KMS, and non-sensitive routes on Hosted. routing policies support that.
06:52 Priya: how about data residency — we need EU-only for certain datasets. can Redwood Hosted pin region?
06:58 Aisha: yes, we have region-backed hosted clusters (EU-only) and Dedicated/Private can be deployed inside your VPC regionally. we'll include region options in the pilot plan.
07:08 Jared: procurement question — how are overages handled on Dedicated?
07:12 Aisha: Dedicated has committed throughput; overages bill at a higher overage rate or we can allow burst capacity at negotiated rates — we can put hard caps to prevent surprise charges.
07:22 Carlos: one more lever: prefix caching — for example, if 60% of the prompt tokens are stable system prompts or long context that repeats, and we cache KV pairs at serve time, we only pay for new tokens. in practice we see 20-50% token reduction on search/assistant workloads.
07:37 Priya: interesting, our product has a set of boilerplate system prompts; that could be big.
07:41 Jared: are there any examples of customers with similar shape who went Dedicated and saw >50% cost reduction?
07:47 Aisha: yes, we can redact names but we've onboarded a mid-market SaaS with steady QPS and they reduced unit cost by ~45% after reserved capacity + int8 quant + caching. we'll send the case study.
07:57 Emily: procurement — we'll need contract language around data handling and termination. can you share a sample SOW for a 3-month pilot?
08:03 Aisha: yes, we'll attach a pilot SOW and standard T&Cs.

08:08 (Carlos begins a technical micro-demo explanation)
08:10 Carlos: demo-style: assume 100 token avg response. with micro-batching at 30ms, you get almost no perceived latency increase for interactive flows but gain batching efficiency that reduces GPU execution time per token by around 1.3x to 1.8x depending on concurrency. combine that with a 0.4x reduction from effective caching and you get the earlier numbers. caveat: batching helps more at higher QPS; at 12 qps small batches still help because concurrency spikes.
08:36 Jared: would that require changes to our API client?
08:39 Carlos: minimal — use Redwood SDK or REST endpoint; batching is handled server-side but we recommend client hints (timeout/window) to maximize coalescing.
08:47 Priya: any special instrumentation we should add?
08:49 Carlos: add per-request tags for route and prompt-type so we can estimate cache hit rates and map to cost. Redwood Console shows token-level breakdowns and cache hit metrics.
08:58 Jared: good. i want to confirm the pilot acceptance criteria: stay within $25k budget for the pilot month (or show path to within 25k at steady state), p95 < 400ms for interactive routes, and SOC2 docs + KMS plan.
09:10 Aisha: noted. quick caveat — pilot usage might be higher as we run stress tests; we'll estimate a steady-state projection and show sensitivity.
09:17 Emily: procurement wants the pilot pricing in a spreadsheet with what triggers a move to Dedicated and the committed discount tiers.
09:24 Aisha: we'll send that.

09:28 (muted typing)
09:32 Carlos: also thinking about fallbacks — you can tier models: critical route uses 7B int8 on dedicated, non-critical uses 3B hosted cheaper model; Redwood routing handles transparent model substitution.
09:44 Jared: how do we measure quality regression with smaller models?
09:47 Carlos: run held-out prompts and compute similarity metrics and human review tags for edge cases; Redwood Optimize supports regression alerts.
09:55 Priya: any network egress costs we should be mindful of for Private?
09:59 Carlos: Private typically keeps traffic in your VPC so egress is your cloud costs; Hosted has egress billed on standard cloud egress lines but usually small relative to token costs. we'll include a rough egress estimate.
10:12 Jared: ok i think we have the outline. next steps recap?
10:15 Aisha: i'll recap: 1) Aisha sends pilot pricing spreadsheet, SOW, SOC2 + KMS docs (due 2026-06-02). 2) Carlos will run benchmarks once Jared supplies prompts and QPS (benchmarks results due 2026-06-11). 3) Elmwood to review and sign pilot SOW if numbers look good.
10:35 Jared: sounds good. any other questions?
10:38 Emily: can we get examples of dedicated commit sizes and typical discount bands?
10:42 Aisha: yes in the pricing sheet.
10:45 Priya: one more — will we be able to rotate KMS keys regularly as part of the SOW?
10:49 Carlos: yes, rotation is supported in Private/Dedicated flows with customer-managed keys; for Hosted we'll show the guidance and options.
10:56 (wrap-up)
10:58 Aisha: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the benchmark.
11:02 Jared: thanks, appreciate the clarity.
